'''Coralie Colmez''' is a French author and tutor in [[mathematics]] and [[mathematics education]].

==Early life and career==
Coralie Colmez is the daughter of mathematicians [[Pierre Colmez]] and [[Leila Schneps]].<ref name="economist">{{cite news |url= https://www.economist.com/prospero/2013/05/02/allow-me-to-explain-your-honour |publisher=[[The Economist]] |title= Allow me to explain, Your Honour |date=2 May 2013 |access-date=2 October 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.thecut.com/2018/01/interview-with-unifrog-founder-coralie-colmez.html |title= The Mathematician Who Moonlights As a Rock-Band Violinist |first=Diana |last=Tsui |publisher=[[The Cut (website)|The Cut]] |date=9 January 2018 |access-date=2 October 2020}}</ref> Colmez was raised in Paris.<ref name="economist"/>

After completing her secondary education in Paris, Colmez moved to the United Kingdom and attended [[Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge|Gonville and Caius College]] of the [[University of Cambridge]] under a Cambridge European Trust scholarship, completing a first-class [[Bachelor of Arts]] in [[Mathematics]] and winning the Ryan Prize in Higher Mathematics.<ref>{{citation
  |access-date=2014-01-05
  |publisher=Andrew Lownie Literary Agency
  |title=Coralie Colmez Biography
  |url=http://www.andrewlownie.co.uk/authors/coralie-colmez
   }}</ref>

==Professional==
Colmez worked for one year as a research assistant on [[Carol Vorderman]]'s task force, commissioned by the UK government to study the state of [[mathematics education]] in the United Kingdom,<ref>{{citation
  |author1=Vorderman, Carol
  |author2=Porkess, Roger
  |author3=Budd, Chris
  |author4=Dunne, Richard
  |author5=Rahman-Hart, Pepe
  |year=2011
  |title=A world-class mathematics education for all our young people
  |url=http://www.conservatives.com/News/News_stories/2011/08/~/media/Files/Downloadable%20Files/Vorderman%20maths%20report.ashx
  |access-date=2013-12-22
   }}</ref> and assisted with the presentation of the findings to the [[Joint Mathematics Council]].<ref>{{citation
  |access-date=2014-01-02
  |publisher=Joint Mathematical Council of the United Kingdom
  |year=2010
  |title=Minutes of JMC Council Meeting held at the Royal Society
  |url=http://cme.open.ac.uk/cme/JMC/JMC%20Minutes%2023rd%20February%202010.htm
   }}</ref> She is now a co-director of [http://www.unifrog.org/ ''unifrog''], an organization that helps students discover future career pathways, apprenticeships and university courses, and teachers track their progress.<ref>{{cite web
  |access-date=2014-01-26
  |publisher=Schools Improvement Net
  |title=Decision time: are your students choosing the best universities for them?
  |url=http://schoolsimprovement.net/decision-time-are-your-students-choosing-the-best-universities-for-them/
  |date=2013-06-11}}</ref>

==Writing==
[[File:Coralie Colmez lecturing students.jpg|right|thumb|Coralie Colmez addressing students]]
With her mother, mathematician [[Leila Schneps]], Colmez co-authored ''[[Math on Trial|Math on Trial: How Numbers Get Used and Abused in the Courtroom]]''.<ref name=motbook>{{citation
  |author1=Schneps, Leila
  |author2=Colmez, Coralie
  |location=New York
  |publisher=Basic Books
  |year=2013
  |isbn=978-0465032921
  |title=Math on Trial: How Numbers Get Used and Abused in the Courtroom
   }}</ref> This book, published in 2013 by Basic Books, targeted for a general audience, uses ten historical legal cases to show how mathematics, especially statistics, can affect the outcome of [[Criminal procedure|criminal proceedings]], especially when incorrectly applied or interpreted. In 2022 Coralie published The Irrational Diary of Clara Valentine, a YA novel which includes high level mathematical concepts with the aim to introduce them to younger readers.

==Public speaking==
[[File:Coralie Colmez at QEDcon 2014.jpg|right|thumb|Coralie Colmez speaking at QEDCon conference in 2014]]
Since the publication of ''Math on Trial'', Colmez has been an invited speaker at scientific education events in the UK. She has presented to the [[Conway Hall Ethical Society]],<ref>{{citation
  |date=2013-12-20
  |title=Sunday Lecture: Maths on Trial - How Numbers Get Used and Abused in the Courtroom
  |url=http://conwayhall.org.uk/51/+/437
  |journal=Conway Hall Ethical Society
   }}</ref> the [[Cambridge Centre for Sixth-form Studies|Cambridge Centre for Sixth-Form Studies]],<ref>{{citation
  |date=2013-12-22
  |publisher=Cambridge Centre for Sixth-form Studies
  |title=Maths trip to Stephen Hawking\'s Lecture Theatre
  |url=http://www.ccss.co.uk/news,maths-trip-to-stephen-hawkings-lecture-theatre_255.htm
  |access-date=2014-03-09
  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140309183640/http://www.ccss.co.uk/news,maths-trip-to-stephen-hawkings-lecture-theatre_255.htm
  |archive-date=2014-03-09
  |url-status=dead
   }}</ref> several shows for Maths Inspiration, including one at the [[University of Cambridge]],<ref>{{citation
  |date=2013-12-21
  |publisher=University of Cambridge
  |title=Maths Inspiration show
  |url=http://www.talks.cam.ac.uk/talk/index/49101
  |journal=Millennium Mathematics Project
   }}</ref> and the 2014 ''[[Merseyside Skeptics Society|QED]]'' conference.<ref>{{citation
  |number=2014–01–05
  |publisher=Lanyrd
  |year=2014
  |title=QED 2014 speakers
  |url=http://lanyrd.com/2014/qedcon/speakers/
   }}</ref><ref>{{citation
  |number=2013–12–22
  |publisher=North West Skeptical Events Ltd
  |year=2013
  |title=Who is speaking at QED?
  |url=https://qedcon.org/speakers/
  |access-date=2014-03-09
  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140807053653/https://qedcon.org/speakers/
  |archive-date=2014-08-07
  |url-status=dead
   }}</ref>  She has appeared on BBC Radio 4's ''Today Programme'', discussing her book's subject of criminal trials in which math is used incorrectly or insufficiently,<ref>{{cite web
  |access-date=2014-01-26
  |publisher=BBC Radio 4
  |year=2013

  |url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b01rg21w/live

  |url-status=dead
  |archive-date=March 31, 2013
  |volume=2014}}</ref> and on the BBC Radio 4 podcast, ''More or Less'', discussing the same topic in relation to the [[Amanda Knox]] case.<ref>{{cite journal
  |author1=Harford, Tim
  |access-date=2014-01-26
